newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed, Coltabaco gains.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed, Coltabaco gains.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed after a session that saw Coltabaco, the country's largest cigarette manufacturer, post impressive gains in Bogota and Medellin.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 0.34 percent to close at 13,652.33 on a lackluster volume of 953.6 million pesos, while Bogota's IBB slipped 0.07 percent to end at 869.21 on a volume of 1.94 billion pesos.
The Bogota index was dragged lower by a 1.44 percent drop in the ordinary shares of blue-chip Banco Ganadero, which was heavily traded and ended at 272 pesos per share.
Banco de Colombia also slipped on profit-taking, ending down 0.47 percent at 420 pesos share.

Brokers said foreign funds and local investors had shown strong buying interest in Banco de Bogota, brewer Bavaria SA and Coltabaco, however, fueled at least in part by expectations of strong third-quarter earnings.

Coltabaco, which some analysts consider undervalued at current levels, led the day's winners in Bogota by rising 2.65 percent to end at 3,131 pesos per share. It was followed by Banco de Bogota, which gained 0.85 percent to end at 6,051 pesos a share and Bavaria, which edged up 0.22 percent.
Coltabaco, which has benefitted from this year's cut in consumer cigarette taxes, also led Friday's winners in Medellin, where it gained 3.81 percent to end at 3,130 pesos per share.
Cement manufacturer Cementos Diamante was the second biggest winner in Medellin, ending up 2.35 percent to end the day at 4,350 pesos a share.
